title: GitHub sees tracker-file conflicts that tk's merge drivers resolve locally, and silently stops running PR CI
description:
The epic PR (#11) stopped getting CI runs at 17:37 on 2026-09-19. Six pushes followed, including a code fix; none triggered a pull_request workflow. GitHub status was all green and pushes to main still ran CI.

Cause: GitHub reported the PR as mergeable=false / mergeable_state=dirty. Locally the merge was CLEAN — because this repository resolves .tick/issues/*.json and .tick/activity/activity.jsonl with tk's custom merge drivers (.gitattributes: merge=tick, merge=tick-activity). GitHub has no such drivers, so the same merge is a textual conflict there (k4s.json and activity.jsonl this time), and GitHub does not run pull_request workflows on a PR it considers conflicted.

Nothing said so. The close-out read 'no checks on the head' and held; an operator sees 'CI pending' indefinitely. The only signal was the ABSENCE of runs, which is the hardest kind to notice.

Two parties touch .tick/ on both sides of every epic PR: the run publishes tracker writes to the epic branch, and people triage and file tickets on main. So this will recur on every long epic, not just this one.

Work, cheapest first:
- The run already folds main into the integration branch at run start (k0d). Fold again whenever main moves while an epic PR is open, using the drivers, so GitHub's merge is always a fast-forward-able one.
- Before holding on 'no CI', the close-out should ask GitHub's mergeable_state; 'dirty' is a different hold with a different repair, and it should be named rather than waited out.
- Consider whether activity.jsonl belongs on the default branch at all — an append-only log that both sides write is a conflict generator by construction.

Worked around by folding main into epic/ncv by hand (9a76a1a); mergeable_state went dirty -> clean and CI started.
acceptance_criteria: An epic PR never sits without CI because of a tracker-file conflict GitHub cannot resolve; if it does, the close-out names the conflict rather than waiting on CI
